articles.headlineTranslated: Measles: Concern over the spread of infections within the prefecture; calls for vaccination — Fukuoka Medical Association (published September 30, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks are being confirmed within Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, prompting warnings from the Fukuoka Medical Association. As of the week ending September 20, nationwide 15 measles cases were confirmed, with 12 in Fukuoka—about 80% of the total. The association attributes much of the spread to increased international travel and returnees. Measles, characterized by fever above 39°C and rash, is highly contagious and spreads through airborne transmission. In a press conference on September 30, the association urged vaccination and other measures. Because simple hygiene like handwashing and masking is insufficient for prevention, individuals with symptoms are advised to contact healthcare providers beforehand and seek care promptly. The association specifically calls for vaccination of children who have not completed the routine immunization schedule.

articles.headlineTranslated: Influenza on the rise; 12 measles cases confirmed in Fukuoka (Published on September 28, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Influenza is in the influenza season in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, with weekly reported influenza cases per medical institution rising 1.2-fold to 5.34 in the week ending September 20. The prefecture had already announced the season’s start in early September and urges continued hand hygiene, masking, ventilation, and vigilance to curb transmission. Separately, measles (ha sika) numbers are rising, with 12 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in the same week, bringing the season total to 22 in Fukuoka. Measles symptoms include fever of 39°C or higher and rash. Health officials warn of ongoing spread and reiterate vaccination and pre-screening. Those with suspected measles should contact healthcare facilities before visiting and avoid using public transport when seeking care.

articles.headlineTranslated: [Measles] Four cases confirmed; total of 10 cases in Fukuoka Prefecture this year (Published September 14, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks in Fukuoka Prefecture reach 10 cases this year as of September 14, 2026, with four new infections reported. A woman in her 20s residing in Fukuoka City developed fever, fatigue, sore throat, and rash; genetic testing on September 13 confirmed measles. She had two prior vaccine doses and no overseas travel history. An additional three infections were announced in Fukuoka City and Kurume City, bringing the annual total to 10. Public health authorities emphasize vaccination as a preventive measure, noting that handwashing or masking alone cannot fully prevent spread, and advise individuals with suspected measles symptoms to contact a medical facility and avoid using public transport when seeking care to reduce transmission.

articles.headlineTranslated: First measles case of the year in Yamaguchi Prefecture; a man in his 20s from Fukuoka Prefecture came to the prefecture by Shinkansen.
articles.summary: Measles diagnosed in Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan—the first measles case in the prefecture in 2026. A man in his 20s from Fukuoka City visited Yamaguchi and traveled there by Shinkansen Nozomi 14 (car 1, non-reserved). He developed fever on Sept 9; rash appeared on Sept 12. He disembarked at Shin-Yamaguchi around 9:10 am and sought medical care the same day. PCR testing at the Environmental Health Center confirmed measles. He is currently under medical care in Yamaguchi Prefecture. The case is considered imported to Yamaguchi due to his origin from Fukuoka. Details on exposure, contact tracing, or vaccination status were not provided. Public health authorities have confirmed the case and are monitoring the potential for further spread as of Sept 14, 2026.

articles.headlineTranslated: Flu Already in Epidemic Status; Increases Observed in Saitama; Irregular Outbreaks Continue Since the COVID-19 Era; Measles Infections Also a Concern
articles.summary: Influenza has entered a nationwide epidemic phase earlier than usual, with Saitama Prefecture reporting rising cases since August, and irregular outbreaks continuing since the COVID-19 era. Vaccination typically ramps up from October, so reinforcing basic infection-control measures is essential to curb spread. National surveillance from sentinel medical institutions shows influenza activity surpassing the season-start threshold of 1.00 for August 17–23, reaching 1.11 patients per institution. This season’s early start is the second-earliest since the Infectious Disease Control Act took effect in 1999, following the 2009 season. Measles infections are also cited as a concern, though the body provides no total counts. As of 2026-09-09, public health guidance emphasizes vaccination timing and non-pharmaceutical measures to mitigate transmission during this early phase.

articles.headlineTranslated: Rising measles cases nationwide: What kind of disease is measles? (Learn from the basics)
articles.summary: Measles (rubeola) is rising nationwide in Japan. As of 2026-09-08, more than 500 measles patients have been reported this year, the highest tally since the COVID-19 pandemic era and second to the 2019 national outbreak of 744 cases. The surge is prominent in major urban areas, including Tokyo, while transmission has reached rural areas as well; a cluster occurred in Kagoshima City in March. Hiroshima Prefecture has three confirmed infections. The article presents a Q&A that explains what measles is and outlines key points about the disease. By placing the current outbreak in historical context, it underscores a notable nationwide rise and regional clusters, emphasizing the need for awareness and public health attention, without adding unrelated details.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles: Fifth case in the prefecture this year after developing a fever; used the subway and Nishitetsu trains; Fukuoka (Sept. 7, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles has been confirmed in Fukuoka Prefecture, the fifth case this year, in a man in his 20s from Onojo City. He developed fever on August 28, with rash and conjunctival injection on September 3, and was diagnosed after seeking medical care. The patient had used public transportation in Fukuoka City and surrounding areas, including the subway, Nishitetsu trains, and Nishitetsu buses, indicating local transmission with no overseas travel history. As of September 7, 2026, five measles cases have been reported in the prefecture this year. Public health authorities emphasize that handwashing and masks may not prevent infection; individuals with compatible symptoms should contact healthcare facilities in advance, avoid using public transit, and obtain vaccination beforehand to reduce transmission.
